title: S8 - Admin web workspace and web release
description: Weeks 15-16. Exit: every Android administrator feature works on the web, an automated check keeps the two apps matched, and the web app passes accessibility, security and performance checks and is deployed.
goal: Give administrators the same features on the web as on Android, then harden and release the web app.
entry_criteria: Confirm owners and realistic capacity before starting.
Required predecessor deliverables are available or scheduled in dependency order.

exit_criteria.description: All sprint issues meet their acceptance criteria and completion evidence requirements.
Perform every administrator task side by side in Android and the browser and show the same results and audit records, then open the deployed web app.

demo: Perform every administrator task side by side in Android and the browser and show the same results and audit records, then open the deployed web app.
risks: The two administrator apps can drift apart; the parity check must run in CI before the web pages are built.
Production release depends on the hosted backend from MOT-28.

execution_plan.first_week: Work prerequisites first; review integration and design risks midweek.
execution_plan.second_week: Integrate, execute acceptance checks, fix defects and demonstrate the sprint outcome.
execution_plan.capacity_policy: Estimates are provisional; reserve approximately 20% of actual team capacity for integration and defects.

issues.title: Set the admin parity rule and its automated check
issues.description: Android and web must have the same administrator features. Layout may differ for the screen; capabilities may not. This issue makes that an enforced rule rather than a promise.
issues.requirements: User request, 2026-11-05: web app for therapists and administrators, in TypeScript

functions.description: List every administrator capability with its Android code, web code and tests.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: checkAdminParity
functions.description: Fail CI when an admin_* database function is not used by both apps.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: docs/architecture/ADMIN-PARITY.md lists every administrator capability with its Android code, web code and tests.

scripts/check_admin_parity.py fails when any admin_* database function is not called by both apps. Today there are 10: admin_accounts, admin_activity, admin_clear_photo, admin_links, admin_publish_exercise, admin_set_account, admin_set_exercise, admin_set_link, admin_set_role, admin_summary.
The check runs in Android, web and database CI whenever administrator code or migrations change.
docs/PLAN.md and AGENTS.md state the rule: a new administrator feature ships to both apps in the same change. A web-only bulk action or export counts as a new feature and needs Android too.
Any gap found while building the web pages is added to the matrix and closed in both apps.

issues.description: Match the Android administrator overview and accounts pages, using the larger screen for tables and side panels.

functions.name: showAdminOverview

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: manageAccounts
functions.description: Search, filter, enable or disable accounts, change staff roles and remove photos.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: The overview shows the same counts as Android: accounts, patients, therapists, administrators, disabled accounts, active links, unlinked patients, active and total exercises, sessions this week and pending requests.
Attention items cover unlinked patients, disabled accounts, the catalogue and data requests, and each opens its section. Recent activity is shown.

The directory has server search across name, email, username and ID, filters for All, Patients, Therapists, Admins and Disabled, and loads 50 accounts at a time. Each account shows when it joined, last sign-in, roles and ID.
An administrator can enable or disable an account, grant or revoke the therapist and administrator roles, and remove another account's photo. Every change needs a confirmation that names the account.
As on Android, an administrator cannot change their own account, roles need an active account, and the reason is shown.
A failed load clears sensitive lists instead of showing old data, and the server rejects every action from a non-administrator, proven by a test.

acceptance_criteria.description: Links are grouped by therapist and filtered by Active, Revoked and All. An administrator can pick a therapist and patient to link, unlink, and restore a link, with the same existing-link and limit messages as Android.
The catalogue lists every exercise, including therapist custom exercises, with activate and deactivate.
An administrator can edit the name and English and Filipino instructions and publish a new version, with an unsaved-changes state and a confirmation showing the next version number.
Activity uses the same event wording as Android, filters by Accounts, Links, Catalogue, Clinical and Privacy, loads older events and labels system events.
Every row in docs/architecture/ADMIN-PARITY.md is marked done with tests on both apps, and the same action in either app writes the same audit record.

acceptance_criteria.description: Profile details can be edited with the same validation as Android, through save_my_profile.
Photos are prepared as JPEG in the browser within the Android size limit and uploaded through profile_photo_upload. The Cloudinary API secret never reaches the browser.
A photo can be removed, and the avatar updates across the app.
Changing the password requires the current password and a different new password that meets the account rules.

issues.title: Complete web accessibility, security, performance and design QA
issues.description: Prove the web app is usable, safe and as polished as designed before it goes live.
issues.requirements: User request, 2026-11-05: web app for therapists and administrators, in TypeScript

functions.name: auditAccessibility
functions.description: Run automated and keyboard-only accessibility checks on every page.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: verifyRoleIsolation
functions.description: Prove with browser tests that each role reaches only its own data.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: reviewBuiltDesign

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: Automated axe checks pass on every page, and a keyboard-only walkthrough covers both workspaces, to WCAG 2.1 AA.
Browser tests prove no therapist reaches administrator pages or another therapist's patients, and no patient reaches either workspace.
Content Security Policy, HSTS and frame-denial headers are set. Patient data never appears in URLs beyond IDs, browser storage, logs or analytics.
Lighthouse scores at least 90 for performance and accessibility on sign-in, therapist home and accounts.
The app works in the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari from 768 to 1920 px wide.
Design QA compares each built screen with the approved designs, and every difference is fixed or approved.
Therapist and administrator usability reviews are recorded in docs/validation/POST-IMPLEMENTATION-CHECKLIST.md and are not claimed as passed until they have been run.

acceptance_criteria.description: The hosting choice is recorded in docs/PLAN.md, and preview and production deployments both work over HTTPS.
Production uses the hosted Supabase project, with its Auth site URL and allowed URLs set for the web address.
Migrations, including 202611050001_custom_exercises.sql, are applied before each release that needs them.
docs/operations/WEB-DEPLOYMENT.md covers release, rollback and monitoring, and a rollback has been rehearsed.
Error monitoring is in place and records no patient data.
